SingleStore

Source: vignettes/singlestore.Rmd
singlestore.Rmd

SingleStore is a SQL database available on your own infrastructure or as the hosted SingleStore Helios service. oauth_db_singlestore() connects with each Shiny visitor’s JWT access token. SingleStore maps the token to a database user and applies that user’s database privileges.

The helper returns a DBI connection. You can query tables with SQL or dbplyr, using the same permissions as the visitor’s other SQL clients. It selects MySQL’s SQL translations and identifier quoting for dbplyr.

Before running the app

Install odbc in R and SingleStore Connector/ODBC 1.2.1 or later for your R architecture. Use odbc::odbcListDrivers() to find its registered name, normally SingleStore ODBC Unicode Driver. The SingleStore driver has its own installation requirements, including the Linux glib and libsecret libraries.

Ask your database administrator to configure SingleStore to trust your provider’s JWT access tokens and map them to database users. The example uses SingleStore 8.1.20 or later, which can select the database user from the JWT when the SQL username is *.

Setting Where to find it
SQL endpoint and port SingleStore workspace or self-hosted aggregator connection details
Database A database the visitor is allowed to query
CA certificate file Trusted PEM CA chain for the SQL endpoint; use the certificate bundle supplied for your deployment
OAuth issuer The sign-in provider whose signing keys SingleStore trusts
Client ID and secret Your OAuth app registration
Access scope and audience The provider configuration agreed with your database administrator

Register http://localhost:8100 as the redirect URI. Configure the provider to issue JWT access tokens for the database and allow token renewal. The database.read scope below is an example; define or replace it for your provider. If the provider requires an audience request parameter, configure that in shinyOAuth’s provider settings.

Save the settings in .Renviron and restart R:

OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-shiny-app-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-shiny-app-client-secret
OAUTHDB_SINGLESTORE_ISSUER=https://login.example.org/realms/reporting
OAUTHDB_SINGLESTORE_SCOPE=database.read
OAUTHDB_SINGLESTORE_SERVER=your-workspace.example.singlestore.com
OAUTHDB_SINGLESTORE_DATABASE=reporting
OAUTHDB_SINGLESTORE_SSL_CA=/path/to/ca.pem

A complete app

This app displays the database user assigned to the visitor. Replace the query with a table or view they can read after checking the identity.

After signing in, click Load rows. The app starts its workers once and stops them at shutdown.

pkgs <- c("shiny", "shinyOAuth", "shinyOAuthDB", "mirai", "odbc")
for (pkg in pkgs) {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(pkg)
  }
}

library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

scope <- Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_SINGLESTORE_SCOPE")

provider <- oauth_provider_oidc_discover(
  issuer = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_SINGLESTORE_ISSUER")
)

client <- oauth_client(
  provider,
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100",
  scopes = c("openid", "profile", "offline_access", scope),
  required_scopes = scope
)

ui <- oauth_ui(
  fluidPage(
    actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
    actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
    actionButton("load", "Load rows"),
    tableOutput("rows")
  ),
  id = "auth",
  client = client
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server(
    "auth",
    client,
    auto_redirect = FALSE,
    async = TRUE
  )
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())
  con <- oauth_db_singlestore(
    auth$connection,
    server = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_SINGLESTORE_SERVER"),
    database = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_SINGLESTORE_DATABASE", "reporting"),
    ssl_ca = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_SINGLESTORE_SSL_CA"),
    required_scopes = scope
  )
  query_task <- oauth_db_task(con)
  observeEvent(input$load, {
    query_task$invoke("SELECT CURRENT_USER() AS database_user")
  })
  output$rows <- renderTable(query_task$result())
}

runApp(
  shinyApp(ui, server, uiPattern = ".*", onStart = function() {
    mirai::daemons(2)
    onStop(function() mirai::daemons(0))
  }),
  port = 8100,
  launch.browser = FALSE
)

# Open the app in your regular browser at its registered redirect URI.

Save the app as example.R, run source("example.R"), and open http://localhost:8100 in a regular browser. Embedded IDE viewers cannot complete the OAuth redirects. For a custom SQL port, add port = 3307L with the port supplied by your administrator.

Configure database access

Follow SingleStore’s JWT setup for self-managed databases or Helios. Configure trusted signing keys, the required audience and a username claim such as sub or email. SingleStore’s jwks_username_field setting selects that claim. Use a signing-key endpoint dedicated to the trusted provider and check the claim requirements for your database release.

Create JWT-authenticated database users and grant their data privileges. For example, an administrator could configure one reader with:

CREATE USER 'analyst@example.org'@'%'
  IDENTIFIED WITH authentication_jwt REQUIRE SSL;
GRANT SELECT ON reporting.* TO 'analyst@example.org'@'%';

The provider must issue the matching username in the configured claim. Signing in to the Helios portal alone does not make an arbitrary OAuth token usable for SQL. The helper uses your shinyOAuth access token and keeps the driver’s separate browser SSO and keyring features disabled.

By default, user = "*" lets SingleStore select the JWT’s database user. To request an explicit user, pass user = "analyst@example.org"; it must match SingleStore’s JWT mapping. A reactive user function can follow a selected account or role. JWT users require SingleStore 7.8.3 or later; using the default wildcard username requires 8.1.20 or later.

TLS and connection lifetime

The ssl_ca file is required. The helper supplies it as SSLCA and sets SSLVERIFY=1, so the driver requires TLS and checks the server certificate and hostname. Supply the CA chain for your deployment, including a private CA when applicable.

Create the helper inside server() and call connection <- con() before each operation. When the access token changes, the next call replaces the connection. Completed reactive queries do not rerun just because a token renews. Changing the account or requested username, signing out, losing required permissions or ending the Shiny session closes the connection.

Automatic driver reconnects are disabled. A driver-reported invalid connection is reopened with a current token. Finish pending results and transactions before obtaining another connection after token renewal. The helper doesn’t replay failed queries. Clear any results your app saves when a visitor signs out or changes accounts, as described in Getting started.
